name: The Dream Team
definition: It's the people. Imagine working alongside stunning colleagues who are great at what they do, and even better at working together.

rows.situation: An open role on the team
rows.under: Fills the seat with someone pleasant and available, and does not ask whether they are great at the work.
rows.justRight: Holds the seat for someone who is great at the work and makes the people around them better.
rows.over: Keeps the seat empty through a long search for a mythical hire while the work piles up on everyone else.

rows.situation: A loved teammate who is no longer the right person
rows.under: Leaves them in the role because the relationship is good, and the work keeps missing.
rows.justRight: Says what the role needs now, helps them move if there is a real fit elsewhere, and changes the seat when there is not.
rows.over: Swaps people out to look decisive, including people who are still the right ones for the work.

rows.under: Treats each person's output as the whole job and lets handoffs stay rough.
rows.justRight: Expects people who are great at the work to make the joint work better, and says so when they do not.
rows.over: Demands so much joint process that the strong people spend the week coordinating instead of doing the work.

rows.situation: A team that gets along and ships average work
rows.under: Calls the harmony a success and leaves the bar where it is.
rows.justRight: Treats average work as a problem even when the team is kind, and raises the bar without making kindness optional.
rows.over: Turns every friendly week into a performance review and people stop telling each other the truth.

rows.situation: Trying to make the workplace attractive
rows.under: Adds perks and leaves the roster as it is.
rows.justRight: Spends the effort on who is in the room. Perks are fine. They are not the point.
rows.over: Refuses ordinary help, tools, or a decent workspace because only the roster is allowed to matter.
